'''Armed conflicts and attacks'''
*[[Somali Civil War (2009–present)|Somali Civil War]]
**[[November 2021 Mogadishu bombing]]
***A [[car bomb]]ing targeting a [[United Nations|UN]] [[convoy]] explodes outside a school in [[Mogadishu]], killing eight people and injuring 17 others. [[Jihadist]] group [[al-Shabaab (militant group)|al-Shabaab]] claims responsibility for the attack. [https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2021/11/25/large-explosion-rocks-somali-capital-mogadishu (Al Jazeera)]
*[[Piracy in the Gulf of Guinea]]
**[[Royal Danish Navy]] [[frigate]] [[HDMS Esbern Snare (F342)|HDMS ''Esbern Snare'']] opens fire and kills four [[pirate]]s in the [[Gulf of Guinea]] after being fired upon. Four other pirates are detained and taken aboard by [[Frogman Corps (Denmark)|Frogman Corps]]. The incident took place 25 to 30 [[nautical mile]]s south of the [[Territorial sea|territorial boundary]] of [[Nigeria]]. [https://www.reuters.com/world/danish-frigate-kills-four-suspected-pirates-gulf-guinea-2021-11-25/ (Reuters)]
*At least 35 people are killed during an eight-day fight over a dispute about [[camel]] [[looting]] between [[herder]]s in Jebel Moon, [[Darfur]], [[Sudan]]. Sixteen villages and thousands of homes are also [[Arson|set on fire]]. [https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2021/11/25/dozens-killed-in-clashes-in-sudans-restive-darfur (Al Jazeera)]

'''Disasters and accidents'''
*[[Listvyazhnaya mine disaster]]
**A fire inside a [[coal mine]] in [[Kemerovo Oblast]], [[Russia]], traps 285 [[mining industry of Russia|miners]] underground. Forty-six miners [[mining accident|are killed]] and 49 others are being treated for [[smoke inhalation]] in hospital. Five rescuers later die while searching for trapped miners, bringing the total death toll to 51. [https://www.dw.com/en/russia-over-50-miners-die-in-siberian-incident/a-59926879?maca=en-rss-en-top-1022-rdf (DW)] [https://www.cbc.ca/news/world/siberia-coal-mine-fire-1.6261971 (CBC)]

'''Health and environment'''
*[[COVID-19 pandemic]]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in Europe]]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Spain]]
****The [[High Court of Justice of Catalonia]] approves the use of the [[COVID-19]] [[immunity passport]] for restaurants, bars and fitness centers in the region. [https://elpais.com/espana/catalunya/2021-11-25/la-justicia-avala-el-pasaporte-covid-en-bares-restaurantes-y-gimnasios-catalanes.html (''El País'')]
****Establishments in [[Aragon]], such as restaurants and nightclubs, begin requiring certificates of immunity for entry. [https://www.expansion.com/economia/2021/11/25/619f3837468aeb9e5c8b45f5.html (''Expansión'')]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in the Czech Republic]]
****The [[Government of the Czech Republic|government]] declares a 30-day [[state of emergency]] and imposes new measures that will require bars and restaurants to close at 10 p.m., bans alcohol consumption at bars and restaurants, restricts the number of people at gatherings and events and bans [[Christmas market]]s. These measures will take effect tomorrow. [https://english.radio.cz/czech-government-declares-state-emergency-8735020 (Radio Prague International)]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in France]]
****The [[France|French]] [[Minister of Health (France)|Minister of Social Affairs and Health]] announces a nationalized plan to provide a third [[booster dose]] of the COVID-19 vaccines to all adults beginning on 27 November, instead of enacting another nationwide state of lockdown in order to reduce the currently record-breaking spread of COVID-19. [https://apnews.com/article/coronavirus-pandemic-health-europe-france-467c6de9c305f7e4df1b53749b2efd23 (Associated Press)]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Germany]]
****[[Germany]] surpasses 100,000 deaths from COVID-19 and also reports a record 75,961 new cases of COVID-19 in the past 24 hours. [https://abcnews.go.com/Health/wireStory/germany-latest-country-pass-100000-deaths-covid-19-81388897 (ABC News)]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in the United Kingdom]]
****The [[United Kingdom]] surpasses 10 million cases of COVID-19. [https://www.itv.com/news/2021-11-25/more-than-10-million-covid-cases-recorded-in-uk-since-the-start-of-pandemic (ITV News)]
***[[European Union response to the COVID-19 pandemic]]
****[[Travel during the COVID-19 pandemic]]
*****The [[European Commission]] issues recommendations that the issuance of the [[EU Digital COVID Certificate]] be shortened to nine months with a requirement to receive a [[booster dose]]. Furthermore, the commission recommends the acceptance of all [[COVID-19 vaccine]]s listed under the Emergency Use Listing by the [[World Health Organization]], including Chinese and Indian-produced vaccines. [https://www.reuters.com/world/europe/eu-recommend-covid-passes-last-nine-months-after-full-vaccination-2021-11-25/ (Reuters)]
****[[COVID-19 vaccine]]
*****The [[European Medicines Agency]] officially approves the use of the [[Pfizer–BioNTech COVID-19 vaccine]] for children between the ages of 5 and 11 years, becoming the first vaccine to be approved for these age groups in Europe. [https://www.msn.com/en-us/health/medical/eu-regulator-authorizes-pfizer-s-covid-vaccine-for-kids-5-11/ar-AAR7F8F?ocid=BingNews (Associated Press)]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in Australia]], [[COVID-19 vaccination in Australia]]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Victoria]]
****The number of people who have received a second dose of the COVID-19 vaccine in [[Victoria (Australia)|Victoria]] surpasses 90%. [https://7news.com.au/lifestyle/health-wellbeing/victoria-reaches-90-per-cent-double-dose-covid-vaccinated-on-thursday-as-cases-rise-c-4693592 (7 News)]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in Argentina]], [[COVID-19 vaccination in Argentina]]
***[[Argentina]] receives 2.5 million doses of the COVID-19 vaccine, which includes 1.1 million doses of the [[Pfizer–BioNTech COVID-19 vaccine]] and 1.3 million doses of the [[Oxford–AstraZeneca COVID-19 vaccine]]. [https://andigital.com.ar/interes-general/item/101172-argentina-recibe-otras-2-5-millones-de-vacunas (ANDigital)]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in Laos]]
***[[Laos]] reports a record 1,504 new cases of COVID-19 in the past 24 hours, thereby bringing the nationwide total of confirmed cases to 67,322. [https://www.laotiantimes.com/2021/11/25/laos-confirms-1504-new-cases-of-covid-19/ (''The Laotian Times'')]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in South Africa]], [[SARS-CoV-2 Omicron variant]]
***[[South Africa]]n scientists detect a new [[Variants of SARS-CoV-2|COVID-19 variant]] named Lineage B.1.1.529 that poses a "major threat" to efforts to reduce the spread of the virus, and blames the variant for the exponential rise of new cases in the country. [https://www.dw.com/en/south-africa-scientists-detect-new-covid-19-variant/a-59934908 (Deutsche Welle)]
*The latest quinquennial [[National Family Health Survey]] in [[India]] finds that the population's [[total fertility rate]] has dropped to a point [[Sub-replacement fertility|below the key replacement rate]] for the first time in the nation's history. [https://www.msn.com/en-us/news/world/india-says-nationwide-birth-rates-drop-below-key-replacement-rate/ar-AAR7G3i?ocid=BingNews (''The Washington Post'')]

'''International relations'''
*[[COVID-19 pandemic in Israel]], [[COVID-19 pandemic in Africa]], [[Travel restrictions related to the COVID-19 pandemic]]
**[[Israel]] bans entry of travellers from [[South Africa]], [[Lesotho]], [[Botswana]], [[Zimbabwe]], [[Mozambique]], [[Namibia]] and [[Eswatini]] and discourages its citizens from travelling to those countries due to the emergence of the Lineage B.1.1.529 variant. [https://www.reuters.com/article/health-coronavirus-safrica-israel/israel-restricts-travel-to-southern-africa-over-new-covid-19-variant-idINL8N2SG57K (Reuters)]
*[[Turkey–United Arab Emirates relations]]
**[[Turkey]] and the [[United Arab Emirates]] sign several investment accords during a high-level visit to [[Ankara]] by [[Emirate of Abu Dhabi|Abu Dhabi]] Crown Prince [[Mohammed bin Zayed Al Nahyan]], including a [[$]]10 billion investment fund to support the [[Health care in Turkey|Turkish health]] and [[Energy in Turkey|energy]] sectors. The [[Central Bank of the Republic of Turkey|Turkish]] and [[Central Bank of the United Arab Emirates|Emirati central banks]] also sign a cooperation agreement. [https://www.reuters.com/world/middle-east/turkey-hopes-uae-investment-deals-during-ankara-talks-2021-11-24/ (Reuters)]

'''Law and crime'''
*[[2021 Solomon Islands unrest]]
**Rioters demanding the resignation of [[Solomon Islands]] [[Prime Minister of Solomon Islands|Prime Minister]] [[Manasseh Sogavare]] set fire to buildings in [[Honiara]]'s [[Chinatown]] neighborhood. Protesters have been defying a 36-hour lockdown imposed following unrest yesterday. [https://www.theguardian.com/world/2021/nov/25/honiaras-chinatown-targeted-as-violent-protests-break-out-for-second-day-in-solomon-islands (''The Guardian'')]
**Australia announces that it will deploy [[Australian Federal Police|federal police]] and [[Australian Defence Force]] personnel to [[Honiara]] to aid with riot control and to secure infrastructure sites following a formal request for help from [[Prime Minister of Solomon Islands|Prime Minister]] [[Manasseh Sogavare|Sogavare]]. [https://www.sbs.com.au/news/australia-to-deploy-adf-troops-federal-police-officers-to-help-quell-civil-unrest-in-solomon-islands/28d4c984-0853-49e1-84fc-fd9ad60d2b40 (SBS News)] [https://www.solomontimes.com/news/australia-agree-to-send-troops-and-police-to-solomon-islands-amid-unrest/11290 (''Solomon Times'')]
**Opposition leader [[Matthew Wale]] calls on the prime minister and his government to resign. [https://www.solomontimes.com/news/leader-of-opposition-calling-on-prime-minister-to-resign/11288 (Solomon Times)]
*[[Blasphemy in Pakistan]]
**Four [[Islam in Pakistan|Muslim]] men are [[criminal charge|charged]] with [[blasphemy]], after arguing with an [[Imam]] who refused to make a funeral announcement for a [[Christianity|Christian]] man in the village of Khodi Khushal Singh, [[Punjab, Pakistan|Punjab]], [[Pakistan]]. [https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2021/11/25/pakistan-arrest-blasphemy-mosque-argument-christian (Al Jazeera)]

'''Politics and elections'''
*[[2021 Romanian political crisis]]
**The [[Parliament of Romania]] votes the [[investiture]] of [[Prime Minister of Romania|Prime Minister]] [[Nicolae Ciucă]]'s [[Grand coalition|grand coalition]] [[Ciucă Cabinet|cabinet]], thereby ending nearly the political crisis. [https://www.politico.eu/article/nicolae-ciuca-romania-prime-minister-national-liberal-party-social-democratic-party/ (''Politico'')]
